# Anatomy, Head and Neck, Larynx Vocal Cords

**Authors:** Manick Saran, Bianca Georgakopoulos, Bruno Bordoni

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

The larynx splits into three distinct regions known as the supraglottis, glottis, and subglottis. Within these three regions the cartilage, neurovascular, and musculature are all intertwined to allow the larynx to function as a unit and carry out its many functions. The primary functions of the larynx are voice production, protection of the airway during respiration, and swallowing. The article reviews the most current scientific knowledge on the anatomy and function of the laryngeal-vocal cords system, integrating with the clinic, embryology, and related conditions.
